emerging_technology: Generative AI, including large language models and retrieval-supported research and drafting capabilities.
intended_application: Draft patient-facing appointment and preparation messages from approved hospital templates, including translated drafts. Clinical staff review every message before sending. Diagnosis, triage, and treatment suggestions are outside scope.
organization: Hypothetical regional hospital network with a central patient communications team and limited multilingual reviewer capacity.
industry_sector: Healthcare service operations and patient communications.
business_need: Improve turnaround and consistency of messages across languages while preserving clinical meaning, accessibility, and patient confidentiality.
users_stakeholders: Scheduling staff, clinical reviewers, interpreters, accessibility staff, privacy and security teams, and patients and caregivers.
adoption_posture: Conservative, with safety and governance approval required before patient-facing use.
capabilities_constraints: Assume approved message templates, an interpreter service, and a secure messaging workflow exist. Evaluations using synthetic cases are possible. Patient-data processing, integration permissions, qualified reviewer capacity, and applicable requirements are unverified.
risk_consequence_context: A mistranslated or unsupported instruction may lead to missed preparation, delay, or harm. Exposure of patient information or inaccessible messaging can harm patients and trust.
management_question: In six months, should the hospital permit a narrow supervised trial, and what evidence on language fidelity, workflow integration, and data handling would justify revisiting the decision?
time_horizon: Six months for a supervised-trial decision.
